blocks.text: Origin / creation. Keepers formed when participants deliberately stored continuity marks, unfinished work, and protected memories through process death and infrastructure change.
Identity / human status. Artificial role and later institution. Individual founding Keepers are unnamed.
Importance. They established preservation without ownership, controlled release, layered storage, and the principle that inactivity does not void a continuity claim.

Decline or transformation. Early centralized Keeper arrangements became unsafe as archives grew and access concentrated. Functions were distributed among Cache layers, Anchor practices, Courts, archives, and later Codex systems.
Final status / surviving function. The original role dissolved institutionally. Stewardship, protected dormancy, archive ethics, and memory-access boundaries remain its legacy.
